import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class RateLimiter:
    """Token bucket limiter shared by all workers."""

    capacity: int
    refill_per_second: float
    tokens: float = field(init=False)
    _lock: asyncio.Lock = field(default_factory=asyncio.Lock, repr=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.tokens = float(self.capacity)
        self._last = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()

    async def acquire(self, cost: int = 1) -> None:
        async with self._lock:
            while True:
                now = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
                elapsed = now - self._last
                self._last = now
                self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + elapsed * self.refill_per_second)
                if self.tokens >= cost:
                    self.tokens -= cost
                    return
                await asyncio.sleep((cost - self.tokens) / self.refill_per_second)

vectors.text:
Great question. The short answer is that caching helps most when many requests share a long, identical prefix, such as a system prompt with detailed instructions or a large document that several questions refer to.

When a request arrives, the provider checks whether the beginning of the prompt matches something it has processed recently. If it does, those tokens are read from the cache instead of being computed again, which is both faster and cheaper. The rest of the prompt, the part that changes from request to request, is processed normally.

There are a few practical consequences. First, put the stable content at the start and the variable content at the end. Second, keep the cached part byte-for-byte identical: even a changed timestamp or a reordered list breaks the match. Third, remember that caches expire after a few minutes of inactivity, so the savings depend on traffic patterns as well as prompt design.

In our measurements, a support assistant with a 6,000-token system prompt saw its average input cost fall by roughly 70 percent after we reorganised the prompt this way.
